title: Redwood Optimize Conductor — Launch Playbook and PRD
author: Priya Nandakumar
content:
Overview:

This document describes the Redwood Optimize Conductor ("Conductor") product: a control plane and policy engine that coordinates hybrid caching, predictive batching, and spot/dedicated capacity selection to reduce per-token cost while preserving route-level latency SLOs. It contains the product goals, an actionable PRD (requirements), high-level design notes, launch roadmap and milestones, pricing & packaging considerations, and a pre-launch release checklist with post-launch telemetry targets.

Audience:
- Product managers, engineering leads (serving runtime, platform, infra), SRE, Finance, Sales Engineering.

Goals and success metrics:
- Primary goal: reduce hosted per-token cost by 25–40% on eligible workloads while keeping 95th percentile latency regression < 5% for SLO-bound routes.
- Success signal 1 (economic): 30% average unit-cost reduction on pilot tenants after 60 days.
- Success signal 2 (reliability): No more than two customer-impacting incidents attributable to Conductor logic in the first 90 days.
- Success signal 3 (adoption): 10% of mid-market customers opt into Conductor during onboarding within 3 months of GA.

Scope (what Conductor includes):
- Policy engine to select routing target (hot cache, hybrid-prefetch, dedicated pool, spot burst).
- Predictive batch size recommendation per route based on historical sequence-length distribution and recent latency tail.
- Prefix/KV cache coordination across regional edges and origin inference pools.
- A lightweight feedback loop that observes trace-level latency and quality regressions and auto-escapes to safe routing.

Out-of-scope for initial launch:
- Full multi-tenant cross-customer cache merging (privacy/legal constraints).
- Deep model-weight-level quantization orchestration (left to Optimize "profiles").

PRD: Requirements (priority ordering)
1) Must-have (MUST):
- Per-route policy definitions: routing_policy, cost_sensitivity (low/medium/high), latency_slo_ms, fallback_sequence.
- API to opt routes into Conductor (console and API) with dry-run mode where Conductor recommendations are visible but not enforced.
- Real-time decision path with 95th percentile decision latency < 5 ms under normal load.
- Safe-escape: automatic switch to pinned model variant or dedicated pool on quality/latency regression above configured thresholds.
- Audit trail: every routing decision persisted for 72 hours with request-id, decision-reason, model-variant, and metrics snapshot.

2) Should-have (SHOULD):
- Predictive batch calculator that outputs recommended batch window (ms) and max tokens per batch for each route.
- Cost impact estimator in Console showing estimated monthly savings per route for a given policy.
- Toggle to force Conductor off for a tenant or route.

3) Nice-to-have (COULD):
- Auto-suggestion engine that proposes quantization profiles or cache TTL adjustments when cost/quality tradeoffs are detected.
- Integration with Sales/Support UI to expose Conductor decisions for troubleshooting in customer QBRs.

Non-functional requirements:
- Security: Conductor data storage must respect tenant isolation and support customer-configured KMS for any persisted decision logs classified as PII.
- Observability: end-to-end tracing, per-decision metrics, and dashboards for cost-savings, safety escapes, and decision latency.
- Scalability: system must handle global peak of 200k decision/sec across all tenants with < 5 ms p95 decision latency.

Design notes (high-level):
- Architecture: stateless decision workers behind autoscaling group, backed by a sharded metadata store (read-optimized) and a time-series metrics cache for recent latency distributions.
- Fallback strategy: hierarchical fallbacks \u2014 route-pin > regional-dedicated-pool > hosted-compatible-variant > model-less-graceful-deny (with informative error).
- Decision determinism: decisions should be stable for a given route and request fingerprint for at least 60 seconds to avoid oscillation. Use leaky-bucket smoothing on metric inputs.
- Safety signals: percent-of-regression, cohort-based quality checks (small closed prompt-sets), sudden tail-latency spikes, and model-decoder anomalies. Any signal above configured thresholds triggers safe-escape.

Operational considerations and ownership:
- Product owner: Priya Nandakumar.
- Engineering owner: Serve Runtime team (lead: Ethan Cole).
- SRE on-call: eng-sre rotation for Conductor namespace.
- Launch readiness gate: security audit OK, performance load test pass, console UX validated, pricing SKU approved by Finance.

Roadmap & Milestones (quarterly):
- Q2 2026: Alpha pilot with 3 internal customers; CLI + Console dry-run, basic telemetry dashboards.
- Q3 2026: Beta with 12 customers, cost estimator in Console, opt-in via API, and two-week pilot feedback loop.
- Q4 2026: GA with SLA advisory, pricing package, and integration with Redwood Optimize GUIs for recommendations.

Launch playbook (step-by-step):
1) Pre-launch (4 weeks before pilot):
   - Complete security review and threat model.
   - Run scale perf test: 200k decisions/s with p95 < 5ms.
   - Prepare console flows and in-product help text.
   - Create customer-facing FAQ and rollback plan.
2) Pilot (030 days):
   - Onboard first 3 tenants in dry-run. Collect telemetry daily; review weekly.
   - Validate cost estimator accuracy vs observed costs.
   - Run red-team scenarios for failure modes (metrics feed loss, sudden model slowdowns).
3) Beta (3038 days):
   - Expand auto-enforcement to small percentage of eligible traffic (530 25%).
   - Require Sales Eng and Customer Success to join weekly reviews for each tenant.
4) GA (after signoff):
   - Turn on default enroll flow for eligible routes with clear console controls.
   - Publish Pricing and packaging (see section below).

Pricing & packaging considerations:
- Pricing intent: Customers see value in predictable, shared savings instead of per-token credits. We propose two packaged options for GA:
  1) Opt-in Savings Split (OSS): Redwood charges a 20% share of documented gross savings on eligible routes. Suitable for self-serve customers.
  2) Commitment-tiered Discount (CTD): Customers commit to a monthly reserved usage tier; Redwood guarantees a target unit-cost reduction and discounts base per-token price in return.
- Billing signals required: Baseline cost model (what the route would have spent without Conductor) must be reproducible and auditable. Finance must own the baseline calculation.
- SKU naming examples for billing: OPT-CONDUCTOR-OSS, OPT-CONDUCTOR-CTD-M (medium), OPT-CONDUCTOR-CTD-L (large).
- Early adopter promotion: first 3 months free Conductor recommendations (dry-run) + 10% discount on OSS share for first year.

Console and observability (UX notes):
- New Console panels: 
  - Route Insights: decision breakdown, estimated savings, and safety escapes.
  - Dry-Run Explorer: playback of recent decisions and "what-if" toggles to simulate policy changes.
  - Audit Trail Viewer: filtered search by request-id, tenant, decision-type.

Launch checklist (pre-GA criteria):
- [ ] Security & privacy signoff (legal + sec).
- [ ] Load test pass (p95 < 5ms at global peak).
- [ ] Console UX validated in user testing (N=6).
- [ ] Billing baseline reproducible demo with Finance signoff.
- [ ] Documentation: KB, QSG, and troubleshooting runbook.
- [ ] Incident playbook tested in game-day.

Release notes (initial Beta release):
- Version: Redwood Optimize Conductor v0.9-beta (2026-04-01)
- Highlights: Dry-run mode, per-route policy & cost estimator in Console, predictive batch recommendation prototype, and audit trail for decisions.
- Known limitations:
  - No cross-tenant cache consolidation.
  - Quantization suggestions are read-only (no auto-rollout).
  - Cost estimator uses sampled traces and may under/over-estimate by up to 15% on highly volatile routes.

Post-launch telemetry & dashboards (targets):
- Decision latency: p95 < 5ms (target), p99 < 20ms (acceptable).
- Cost delta accuracy: median error < 10% across pilot tenants.
- Safety escape rate: < 0.5% of requests for enrolled routes after stabilization.
- Customer-reported incidents attributable to Conductor: 0 in 90-day window (target).

Appendices:
A) Example policy JSON (Console and API compatible)
{
  "route_id": "billing-invoice-gen",
  "routing_policy": "latency-first",
  "cost_sensitivity": "medium",
  "latency_slo_ms": "200",
  "fallback_sequence": ["route-pin","regional-dedicated","hosted-variant"],
  "dry_run": true
}

B) Troubleshooting playbook (summary)
1) If decision latency increases:
   - Check metrics ingestion latency and fall back to cached distributions.
   - Scale decision workers (horizontal).
2) If quality regressions observed:
   - Immediately flip disabled flag for tenant, collect paired traces, and escalate to Serve Runtime for model investigation.
3) If cost estimator drift > 20%:
   - Pause auto-enforcement, run recalibration job using 7-day rolling window, inform Finance.
